generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The refactored offset-correction logic for the insertion case (`charDelta > 0`) now emits one `addOffCorrectMap` entry per inserted character instead of a single boundary entry. This is a meaningful semantic change: the old code recorded a single correction at `normalizedCharPos + numChars` with value `lastDiff - charDelta`, while the new code records corrections at `normalizedCharPos + (end - startIter) + i` with value `lastDiff - i` for each `i` in `[0, charDelta)`. Please confirm that downstream consumers of the offset-correction map (e.g., the token-position mapping in `NlpTokenizer.tokenize`) are compatible with receiving multiple adjacent entries rather than a single cumulative one. If the map is expected to hold at most one entry per output position, the loop is correct; if it was previously relying on a single "delta" entry to shift all subsequent positions, the behavior will differ.

The field name `MULTILINUGAL_TEXTS` contains a transposition typo — it should be `MULTILINGUAL_TEXTS` (the "GAL" and "GUAL" are swapped). The same misspelling is repeated in the Javadoc `{@link}` references and in the test method `#X5VWB`. Fixing it now is cheaper than after it becomes part of the public API surface of the test class.

`logger.info(i)` appears to be a leftover debug statement. It logs a bare integer index with no context, which will be noise in test output. Remove it, or if you want per-iteration logging for debugging a failing case, use a more descriptive message (e.g., `logger.debug("tokenizing text index {}", i)`) and gate it at `DEBUG` level.

review_comment: could you extract all this into a resource file. Then this `XLMRobertaTestVocab` could read and parse from that file so that it is easily used by others. Having all this statically used fields seems overly heavy to me.
